subject: Service-provider role decision flow for acquisition data transfers and subprocessor acceptance
messages:
From: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@brightbridge.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightbridge.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify SP/Processor designation for planned BrightBridge acquisition flow

Hi Mina,

Quick note from procurement as we scope the acquisition integration: the legal team is pushing for confirmation that Redwood will only act as a Service Provider / Processor (and not a seller) for telemetry and model inference related to the acquired product. That affects resale/disclosure gating in a couple of states.

Two asks:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood treats the inferred outputs + telemetry from this integration as "sale" under CCPA/CPRA, or if it remains limited-use processing?
- If you rely on subprocessors for inference or telemetry (e.g., cloud partners, monitoring), can you share an up-to-date subprocessor roster and any onshore fallback commitments?

We have a tight internal timeline — would appreciate a short written confirmation we can include in the SOW and the DPA.

Thanks,
Sara Mueller
Head of Procurement, BrightBridge Analytics
---
BrightBridge | procurement@brightbridge.ai
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify SP/Processor designation for planned BrightBridge acquisition flow

Sara — thanks for the clear asks. Short answer up front: Redwood will operate as a Service Provider / Processor for customer data in this integration; we do not re-sell customer personal data or combine it for advertising purposes. We classify telemetry and model inference outputs as limited-use processing under our standard US privacy addendum.

A few specifics and next steps:
1) Sale classification: we do not treat telemetry or generated outputs as a "sale" under CCPA/CPRA in our standard terms. We only perform processing on behalf of the controller (BrightBridge) and adhere to the data handling instructions in the DPA.
2) Subprocessors: attached is our current roster (redwood_subprocessors_2026-11.csv). It lists inference infra partners, metrics/observability providers, and an encryption key manager. We require subprocessors to adhere to contractual terms that match our DPA.
3) Onshore fallback / telemetry locality: we offer an onshore fallback for telemetry and logging for enterprise customers under dedicated capacity or Private deployments (see onshore-fallback-sla-appendix.docx). For hosted integrations, we can provide region-restricted routing and a documented fallback plan (onshore fallback within 72 hours) as part of the Dedicated offer.
4) DPA redlines: Karthik and Jonas are copied — we can accept a limited set of DPA edits, but will need to keep the service-provider/processor language and the limited-use clause intact. If you share the requested redlines, we can produce a tracked version and route for DocuSign.

Attaching: redwood_subprocessors_2026-11.csv; draft DPA available in attachments.

Next step: if procurement can provide the specific DPA redlines and any state-specific carveouts you need, we'll circulate a final track for signature.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Legal & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_2026-11.csv (CSV list), redwood_dpa_draft_20261115.pdf (Draft DPA)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:29:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify SP/Processor designation for planned BrightBridge acquisition flow

Sara / Mina — a couple of legal clarifications from our side:
- Processor boundary: to avoid ambiguity we prefer the DPA to explicitly list the processing activities (inference, telemetry collection for reliability, performance analytics) and a prohibition on selling or targeting. That language helps with state definitions that hinge on downstream commercial use.
- Telemetry minimization: we can commit to retention and minimization defaults (30/90/365 days tiers) depending on deployment; please indicate your preferred retention horizon and we can bake it into the SOW.
- Subprocessor onboarding: we do not require customer approval for the full roster, but for named high-risk subprocessors (e.g., offshore observability vendors), we can provide a 10-business-day notice and an onshore fallback option.

Jonas, can you confirm operationally the 72-hour onshore fallback for telemetry — is that achievable for BrightBridge's expected volumes if we provision Dedicated capacity?

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify SP/Processor designation for planned BrightBridge acquisition flow

Karthik / team — confirmed operationally:
- 72-hour onshore fallback is feasible if BrightBridge commits to Dedicated capacity or Redwood Private. For hosted-only, we can provide region pinning but not guaranteed 72-hour migration without capacity reservation.
- Retention tiers: default telemetry retention is 90 days for hosted, configurable to 30/365 on Dedicated/Private; metrics aggregates can be provided with longer-term retention on request.
- Subprocessor operational note: the CSV lists an offshore observability provider (O-Viz) that we classify as medium risk. If BrightBridge requires avoidance of O-Viz, we can either: (a) switch telemetry to onshore partner (slower provisioning, 10-15 business days) or (b) enable caching at edge so less telemetry is collected.

Operational next step: confirm the desired retention and whether you will choose Dedicated/Private. If you need DocuSign-ready DPA we can push the final at that point.

Jonas Weber
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Derek Connors <derek.connors@brightbridge.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@brightbridge.ai>, procurement@brightbridge.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify SP/Processor designation for planned BrightBridge acquisition flow

Mina — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups from legal and engineering:

1) Legal is asking that the DPA include: explicit limited-use clause, named activities, and a 10-business-day notice for any new subprocessor considered high-risk. They also asked for the redlined DPA to be returned by EOD Thursday.
2) Engineering would prefer not to go Dedicated immediately. Can you confirm the exact differences in guarantees (retention and fallback SLA) between hosted + region pinning vs Dedicated? A short bulleted comparison would help our CTO decide.

We can accept the CSV roster for now but would like the DocuSign package and SOC 2 report to be attached with the final DPA. Can you route the SOC 2 link / report and a DocuSignable DPA?

If we can get the DPA with the requested clauses and SOC 2 link by Thursday EOD, procurement can proceed to the signature window.

Thanks,
Derek Connors
VP Engineering, BrightBridge Analytics
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Derek Connors <derek.connors@brightbridge.ai>, Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightbridge.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify SP/Processor designation for planned BrightBridge acquisition flow

Derek / Sara — we can deliver the requested items by Thursday EOD. Actions below:
- Legal: we will produce a tracked DPA that includes an explicit limited-use clause, named processing activities, and a 10-business-day notice for high-risk subprocessors. Expect the DocuSign package link in my next email.
- Compliance: SOC 2 report link: https://redwood.app/compliance/soc2-report-2026 (view-only, NDA required - I will share the NDA link in the DocuSign packet).
- Ops: short comparison (bullets) attached: hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (I included retention/fallback guarantees).
- Subprocessor request: if you identify any subprocessors from the roster you want restricted, flag them by Wednesday COB and we'll prioritize switching to the onshore partner or enabling edge caching.

I'll route the DocuSign packet with the DPA and NDA for SOC 2 access by Thursday morning.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Legal & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_dpa_draft_20261115.pdf, onshore-fallback-sla-appendix.docx, redwood_subprocessors_2026-11.csv
